decisions.id: W49-3 no seat in the frame: the first seat past the frame's edge
decisions.summary: placer.place: a candidate within the hug but outside the frame is remembered, and when no in-frame candidate exists at all the caption is drawn at the first such seat, past the picture's edge
decisions.why: This is an exception to 0242's own rule, 'A place that would run off the edge of the picture is never taken. A clipped caption cannot be read' and its spec paragraph 'a place off the edge of the picture is never taken' - the same docstring still claims 'never clipped - a seat leaving the picture is never a candidate', now false on this branch, and test_the_frame_is_never_left now asserts the frame is left. The general rule is not physically impossible here: the trigger is 'no seat within the hug (HUG_PX, labeled CONVENTION) lies inside the frame', and 0242 itself names the way on - 'beyond that the caption is tied to its feature by a thin leader line', with no researched limit - so a leader seat past the hug, inside the frame, honors both 'never left off' and 'never off the edge'. The exception breaks a researched rule to keep an unresearched convention, the reverse of FR-004's direction. It also defeats 'never left off''s own purpose: a clipped caption cannot be read, which is the page's reason. And the claim cites 0241 ('there is no key box') for the past-the-frame seat, which 0241 does not say. What would be legitimate: search on past the hug (on a leader) inside the frame before leaving it, and leave the frame only where no seat of the caption's size fits inside the frame at all (the 10 x 10 px frame of the restated test, physically impossible), that residue labeled as such in the claim rather than cited to 0241.
